_meta.note: Natco Pharma: industry, peers, street, ownership, moat, critiques, gaps and conflicts. Only sources published on or before 30-Sep-2026; later facts are in updates/later-facts.json.

usGenerics.text: US generics is a 'winner takes all' market for first-to-file (FTF) para-IV products: the first filer can get 180 days of exclusivity; after that, prices fall 80-90% as more generics enter. Natco's model is to pick hard-to-make or litigated molecules with few filers and partner with a US marketer (Teva, Mylan/Viatris, Breckenridge, Lupin, Dr. Reddy's, Sun, Alvogen) who shares litigation cost and pays a profit share.

usFilerReality.text: CEO (29-May-2026): 'especially if you're doing an NCE-1, chances are most products, you have 8 or 10 or 15 or 20 guys who file on day'; 'if we're able to pull off in a 3 to 4 year time period... even 3 of those, you have done a great job'. FY26: 7-8 US filings, no major FTF.

indiaGlp1.text: Semaglutide went off patent in India in Mar-2026; Natco launched the first generic vial on day one and the pen a month later; 10-15 generics; CEO: 'The market is cutthroat'; own brand ~Rs2 cr a month; vial < Rs1,000 a month vs pen Rs3,000-4,000.

southAfrica.text: Adcock Ingram is the second-largest South African pharma company by private-market share; four divisions (prescription, OTC, hospital, consumer); three plants near Johannesburg and 49% of an Indian JV with two plants.

cropProtection.text: Indian crop-protection market ~US$2.6-2.7 bn (2025-26), projected US$3.36 bn by 2031 (4.45% CAGR); input costs rose 25-30% after the West Asia war (Natco CHS head, 29-May-2026).

brokers.thesis: Loss of gRevlimid exclusivity took a toll on Q4FY26; FY27 is a consolidation year; growth from FY28 on US, Canada and Brazil launches, Adcock and future exclusivities; 'new launches and M&As critical to revive growth'
Healthy Q4 core business without meaningful gRevlimid; FY27/FY28 EPS raised 5%/4%; semaglutide India, Brazil/Canada/US launches; ~Rs2,500 cr cash for deals (target raised from Rs1,035)
Revenue to moderate as Revlimid competition rises; generic Pomalyst and RoW partly offset; semaglutide partnerships lift India; two acquisitions under evaluation (pre-Q4 note)

street.consensusNote: We found no broker note on Natco dated between the Q1FY27 results (14-Aug-2026) and 30-Sep-2026 that we could read. Trendlyne lists no note for that window. A press tracker quotes an S&P Global poll of 11 analysts (consensus Hold, average target Rs1,021, ~19-Jun-2026); we could not open the underlying page and do not use it.

ownership.promoterSrc: AR FY26 consolidated note 15 (vi), holdings at 31-Mar-2026; promoter group total 49.43% at 31-Mar-2026, 49.41% at 30-Jun-2026
ownership.pledge: No promoter pledge disclosed in the AR FY26 shareholding notes (gap: we did not open the Jun-2026 BSE pattern).
ownership.trend: Promoters 48.8% (Mar-21 to Mar-23) rose to 49.7% after the FY24 buyback, then edged down to 49.4% (small family sales: Satya Vani and Sanjay Nannapaneni sold in FY26). DIIs fell from 16.1% (Mar-21) to 5.6% (Jun-26); retail shareholders rose from 85,509 to ~403,000.

rows: Techno-legal skill in para-IV / FTF generics
gRevlimid, Copaxone (glatiramer), Tamiflu, Afinitor: a long record of picking litigated molecules; 28 para-IVs, 17 approvals pending; but FY26 produced no major new FTF
~Rs3,000 cr of revenue without lenalidomide; small next to Sun, Cipla or Dr. Reddy's; relies on partners for US distribution and litigation
Top-3 in the oncology segment it operates in; 10 brands above Rs10 cr; but the domestic business is only Rs441 cr and grew 10% in FY26
Emerging-market front ends (Brazil, Canada, South Africa)
Brazil single source for everolimus for four years; Canada top-10 generic company; Adcock gives the #2 position in South Africa, at 49% only
Kothur warning letter Apr-2024, closed Sep-2025; Mekaguda and Chennai cleared in 2025; Vizag due for inspection
CEO: 'certain businesses are roller coaster'; FY25 EPS Rs104, FY27E ~Rs40
moat.verdict: Natco has a real skill (finding and litigating limited-competition generics) but no durable moat: each exclusivity decays, and the base business that remains is sub-scale. Adcock adds stable earnings but Natco does not control it.

critiques.text: 'Earnings hiccups imminent' as gRevlimid ended; raised to Hold Rs1,000 by May-2026 after a 20% fall in the share price
FY27 profit guidance of ~Rs750 cr includes ~Rs220 cr from Adcock (29% of PAT), a business Natco does not control, at a 49% stake bought at a higher price in July 2026 than in Nov-2025.
Capital allocation: Rs3,000 cr spent on a minority stake, then a Rs1,279 cr rights issue at Rs750 four months later to repay the debt that funded it; management rules out buybacks ('No').

gaps: Lenalidomide (gRevlimid) revenue and profit by year are not disclosed by Natco; our estimates are US revenue less an ex-lenalidomide US base of ~Rs700 cr a year.
Broker notes after the Q1FY27 results (Aug-Sep 2026): none found that we could read; ICICI Securities and Trendlyne PDFs need a login; Business Standard returned HTTP 403 (not bypassed).
ICRA rating rationales (Aug-2025, Nov-2025) need a download form: not used.
Named institutional holders at Jun-2026 (BSE shareholding pattern): not opened; categories from the Q1FY27 presentation.
Natco does not name its FY28 US exclusivity launches (confidentiality); carfilzomib (settlement launch CY2027) is the only one stated.
Adcock Ingram's own audited accounts (delisted Nov-2025) are not public; we use Natco's associate note and call disclosures.
Balance sheet at Jun-2026 (after the July Adcock tranche) is not published; borrowings of ~Rs1,000 cr are our estimate from the rights-issue objects (Rs810.5 cr of named loans).
conflicts: Brazil FY26: Rs287.5 cr (AR FY26 MD&A) vs 'about Rs257 crores... plus some billing directly from India' (CEO, 29-May-2026). We use the AR figure (it includes the India billing).
Canada FY26: Rs251.7 cr (AR FY26) vs Rs229 cr (CEO, 29-May-2026, subsidiary only). We use the AR figure.

FY27 revenue guidance: 'Rs3,400-3,500 crores of revenue' (29-May-2026) vs 'gross sales will be between Rs3,300-3,400 crores' (14-Aug-2026). We read May as total revenue (incl. other income) and August as sales.
The user brief gives trailing EPS to Jun-26 of ~Rs46; the four quarters to Jun-26 sum to Rs63.3 (Screener). Rs45.9 is the trailing EPS to Sep-26, which includes Q2FY27 (after the as-of date).
